title: Open immersions of spaces descend along etale target covers
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $a:X\to P$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $\{P_i\to P\}_{i\in I}$ be a jointly surjective family of etale maps with each $P_i$ a scheme. Suppose each base change $X\times_PP_i\to P_i$ is an open immersion, meaning it is represented by the inclusion of an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Then $a$ is representable and is an open immersion: for every scheme $V\to P$, $X\times_PV$ is a scheme and its projection to $V$ is an open immersion. In particular, if $P$ is a scheme then $X$ is a scheme isomorphic over $P$ to an open subscheme of $P$.

source.place: Tag 03M4 (lemma-closed-immersion-local), open-immersion case, (4) implies (1) and (1) implies (2); also spaces-descent.tex Tag 041X (lemma-descending-property-open-immersion).

proof.text: Fix a scheme test $t:h_T\to P$. Representable etaleness of each $p_i$ supplies a scheme $T_i$, an etale projection $q_i:T_i\to T$, and a cartesian square with other projection $c_i:h_{T_i}\to h_{P_i}$. Apply the local-surjectivity hypothesis to the section $t_T(1_T)$. Its covering fppf sieve is jointly surjective: Scheme.exists_flat_mem_of_mem_fppfTopology supplies, above each point of $T$, an arrow $f:V\to T$ in that sieve and a point of $V$. Give $V$ its induced $S$-structure. A local lift $y\in P_i(V)$ together with $f$ satisfies $p_i(y)=t(f)$ by naturality. The cartesian square gives a map $V\to T_i$ above $f$, hence a point of $T_i$ above the specified point of $T$. Thus the $q_i$ are jointly surjective. Etale morphisms are flat and locally finitely presented, so this is an fppf covering, hence fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. No nonemptiness of the index set is needed.

source.place: Tag 041X, reduction to a scheme target; fppf covering and scheme-test pullback definitions

proof.text: The representable fppf sheaf $h_T$ is an algebraic space: scheme finite limits represent its diagonal, and the identity is its surjective etale atlas. The private Lean helper proves both assertions directly using Yoneda and the definitions. Form $Z=X\times_P h_T$ in sheaves. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] it is an algebraic space. The sheaf forgetful functor preserves this pullback, so its presheaf projections $s:Z\to X$ and $r:Z\to h_T$ give a cartesian square over $a,t$.

source.place: Tag 041X, the space over the scheme test; Spaces Tags 02X2 and 04T9 for fibre-product closure

proof.text: For each $i$, apply the given representable-with-open-immersions condition for $X\times_P P_i\to P_i$ to the scheme test $c_i:h_{T_i}\to h_{P_i}$. It gives a scheme $U_i$, an open immersion $j_i:U_i\to T_i$, and a representing pullback square. Paste this square with the defining square of $X\times_P P_i$. Its bottom map is $c_i p_i=q_i t$. Cancel the cartesian square defining $Z$ to obtain a cartesian square $h_{U_i}\to Z$ over $h_{j_i}:h_{U_i}\to h_{T_i}$ and $h_{q_i}:h_{T_i}\to h_T$. Its canonical pullback isomorphism identifies $Z\times_T T_i$ with $h_{U_i}$ and its projection with $h_{j_i}$. This uses the full scheme-test hypothesis, so no separate scheme open-immersion base-change theorem is needed.

source.place: Tag 041X, local open representatives after a scheme test

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-fpqc-open-immersion-descent] to the algebraic space $Z$, the map $r:Z\to h_T$, and the fpqc scheme cover $(q_i)$ from step 1, with the local representatives from step 3. It supplies a scheme $U$, an open immersion $j:U\to T$, and an isomorphism $e:Z\simeq h_U$ with $r=e\,h_j$. Transport the square of step 2 along $e^{-1}$. Its top map is $h_U\xrightarrow{e^{-1}} Z\xrightarrow{s}X$, its other projection is $h_j$, and it is still cartesian. This is exactly the witness required by IsRepresentableWith for $a$ at the arbitrary test $t$. Thus the theorem follows. The cited descent statement packages support descent and sheaf representation; it is an existing generic tool, not a replacement of a unit step.

source.place: Tag 041X, open-subscheme descent and final identification; Tag 03M4, scheme-test characterization

proof_origin.place: Tag 041X, scheme-test reduction and fpqc open-immersion descent. Stage-3 D9 uses the already stated lem-sfb-space-fpqc-open-immersion-descent as a generic tool to package support descent and representation, with explicit pullback pasting and transport. No unit statement or step is bypassed.

lean.statement: theorem isOpenImmersion_of_etale_cover {S : Scheme.{u}} {X P : AlgebraicSpace S} (a : X ⟶ P) (I : Type u) (P_i : I → Over S) (p_i : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (P_i i) ⟶ P.obj.obj) (h_etale : ∀ i, IsEtale (p_i i)) (h_joint : ∀ (T : Over S) (x : P.obj.obj.obj (Opposite.op T)), ∃ (R : Sieve T.left), R ∈ Scheme.fppfTopology T.left ∧ ∀ (U : Over S) (f : U ⟶ T), R f.left → ∃ (i : I) (y : (yoneda.obj (P_i i)).obj (Opposite.op U)), (p_i i).app (Opposite.op U) y = P.obj.obj.map f.op x) (h_open : ∀ i, AlgebraicSpace.IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ q => IsOpenImmersion q.left) (pullback.snd a.hom.hom (p_i i))) : AlgebraicSpace.IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ q => IsOpenImmersion q.left) a.hom.hom
